part.company: Velankani Information Systems Pvt. Ltd., Bangalore, India

AB_compound.note: Tags A1-A4 and B1-B4 refer to the SAME four hole locations — two diameters at each position

C_precision.note: Four separate Ø5 H7 precision through holes

DE_compound.note: Tags D1-D4 and E1-E4 refer to the SAME four hole locations — two diameters at each position

drawing_interpretation.critical_warning: Do NOT drill 8 separate A-holes and 8 separate B-holes. A and B are two diameters at the same 4 locations. Same applies to D and E. Confirm with design before issuing operation sheet.

dro_coordinates.note: Plate is 95x95 mm. Datum origin set at finished lower-left corner for manual DRO work. Centre = X47.50, Y47.50 from lower-left.

raw_material.rationale: Extra 5 mm on each face dimension useful for clamping during hole machining. Extra 1.5-2 mm on thickness covers roughing and grinding allowance.
requirements: Normalized condition — no hardening unless design specifies
Check flatness before machining — do not load bowed plate onto milling machine

manufacturing_philosophy.approach: Manual-first — use manual machines for the majority of operations. Use CNC only where positional accuracy or size tolerance genuinely demands it.
manual_operations: Four O16 H7 counterbores (manual boring preferred — use CNC as fallback only)
cnc_operations: Four O5 H7 through holes — CNC drilling and reaming for positional accuracy
O16 H7 counterbores — CNC fine boring as fallback when manual boring cannot hold Ø16.000-16.020

process_sequence.name: Raw material preparation
actions: Cut C45 normalized plate to 100 x 100 x 12 mm blank
Remove heavy scale from cut edges
Check for visible bow or twist before proceeding

process_sequence.name: Rough manual milling
process_sequence.machine: VISPL-TLR-003 Manford vertical precision milling machine
sequence: Face-mill first surface lightly — remove scale
Flip and face opposite surface
Alternate faces — remove equal material from both sides to reduce bending
Rough thickness to 10.30-10.40 mm
Mill all four sides square
Rough outside to approximately 95.30 x 95.30 mm
process_sequence.caution: Do not remove all material from one face — thin plate will bow

process_sequence.name: Straightness check and optional stress relief
actions: Check plate on surface plate with dial indicator
If bow is significant — leave overnight and recheck
Stress relieve only if plate repeatedly distorts — may need outsourcing (no heat-treatment furnace listed in equipment master)
process_sequence.note: For small normalized C45 plate stress relief is usually unnecessary unless raw plate was already distorted

process_sequence.name: Finish surface grinding
sequence: Grind first face lightly
Flip and grind opposite face
Alternate sides — do not finish one face completely before touching the other
Light magnetic chuck force — thin plate distorts under heavy magnetic load
Finish thickness to 10.00 mm
checks: Thickness at all four corners and centre
process_sequence.critical_note: All counterbore depths must be machined AFTER surface grinding — depths are measured from the finished face

process_sequence.name: Finish outside dimensions manually
process_sequence.machine: VISPL-TLR-003 Manford vertical precision milling machine
sequence: Return ground plate to milling machine
Finish one side
Flip and finish opposite side parallel
Finish remaining two sides square
Achieve 95.00 x 95.00 mm
process_sequence.note: Finished outside edges become the DRO datum for all subsequent drilling operations

process_sequence.name: DRO drilling setup
process_sequence.machine: VISPL-TLR-004 or VISPL-TLR-005 Eifco drilling machine with DRO
setup: Place sacrificial mild-steel or aluminium plate under component — protects table and reduces exit burrs
Clamp component with low-profile clamps — full support below plate
Use edge finder or dial indicator to establish DRO datum
Set lower-left finished corner as X0, Y0
Centre of plate is X47.50, Y47.50 from lower-left corner
process_sequence.sacrificial_plate_note: Drill clearance holes in sacrificial plate below every through-hole location before clamping

process_sequence.name: Drill O6.4 through holes (4 off) and O8.0 through holes (4 off) on DRO drilling machine
process_sequence.machine: VISPL-TLR-004 or VISPL-TLR-005 Eifco drilling machine with DRO
sequence: Spot all eight locations — A/B and D/E groups only. Do NOT spot C locations if O5 H7 will be CNC-reamed.
Drill four O6.4 through holes at A1/B1 through A4/B4 DRO coordinates
If tighter size required: drill O6.2-6.3 first then ream to O6.40
Drill four O8.0 through holes at D1/E1 through D4/E4 DRO coordinates
Drill O7.8 pilot first then ream to O8.0 for better concentricity and size
Use cutting fluid throughout
Reduce feed as drill exits to minimise exit burr
process_sequence.note: The Ø8 holes also guide the Ø16 H7 counterbore in the next stage

process_sequence.name: Produce O10.4 counterbores (4 off)
process_sequence.machine: VISPL-TLR-003 Manford vertical precision milling machine
process_sequence.specification: O10.40 dia, 6.80 mm deep, over the O6.4 through holes

preferred_method.tool: O10.4 flat-bottom piloted counterbore with O6.4 pilot
procedure: Insert pilot into O6.4 through hole
Touch cutter onto finished face — set Z zero

alternative_method.condition: When piloted counterbore is not available
steps: Locate spindle over O6.4 hole using coaxial indicator or setting pin
Rough with 8 or 10 mm end mill
Finish diameter with small boring head to O10.40
Finish bottom with flat-bottom end mill at 6.80 mm depth
alternative_method.warning: Do not use loose drilling-machine spindle with end mill for this operation

process_sequence.name: Produce O16 H7 counterbores (4 off)
process_sequence.machine: VISPL-TLR-003 Manford vertical precision milling machine (preferred manual method)
process_sequence.cnc_fallback: VISPL-TLR-008 Makino VMC or VISPL-TLR-021 ACE MCV-700 Plus
process_sequence.specification: O16.000 to O16.020 mm, 8.0 mm deep, over O8.0 through holes

steps: Locate spindle accurately over O8 through hole using coaxial indicator or O8 setting pin
Rough with 14 or 15 mm flat-bottom end mill
Finish diameter using fine boring head
Adjust boring head in small increments
Target O16.008-16.012 mm (centred within H7 band)
preferred_manual_method.best_tooling: O16 H7 piloted counterbore with O8.0 pilot and flat-bottom cutting geometry — reduces machining time significantly

cnc_fallback_condition: First manually bored hole is not round or not within O16.000-16.020
Consistent concentricity cannot be maintained manually
process_sequence.procedure: Machine and inspect first hole manually. Continue manually if result is satisfactory. Switch to CNC only if manual result fails.
process_sequence.warning: Do not use an ordinary long-lead reamer for this blind counterbore — reamer chamfer prevents full H7 diameter reaching the shoulder

process_sequence.name: Produce O5 H7 through holes (4 off) on CNC
process_sequence.specification: O5.000 to O5.010 mm through, H7
process_sequence.rationale: These holes require both H7 diameter tolerance and accurate two-decimal coordinate positioning. CNC drilling and reaming is the correct method.
cnc_setup: Clamp finished plate flat on clean fixture or parallels
Set lower-left corner as X0, Y0 (or set plate centre as X0, Y0)
cnc_sequence: Spot drill very lightly — do not make deep spot on H7 holes
Ream with sharp O5 H7 machine reamer
Flood coolant, continuous feed — do not stop or reverse reamer inside hole

use_when: O5 H7 reaming performance cannot be achieved reliably
wedm_alternative.note: For current unhardened C45 plate CNC drilling and reaming is faster and sufficient

process_sequence.name: Deburring and edge finishing
sequence: Remove all drill exit burrs from bottom face
Break outside edges approximately 0.2-0.3 mm
Apply only very small edge break to H7 holes — do not reduce effective guiding length
Do not create large chamfer in O5 H7 or O16 H7 holes
Clean counterbore shoulders and corners
Remove all metal particles before inspection

process_sequence.name: Final inspection
process_sequence.note: Inspect after parts reach ambient temperature

inspection_plan.equipment: Surface plate and dial test indicator
Bore gauge or suitable plug gauge
GO/NO-GO plug gauge or bore gauge

inspection_plan.positions: All 4 holes — check taper and bell-mouth

inspection_plan.equipment: CMM preferred; height gauge + gauge pins on granite surface plate if no CMM

machine_allocation.equipment: VISPL-TLR-004 or VISPL-TLR-005 Eifco drilling machine with DRO
VISPL-TLR-003 Manford vertical precision mill + boring head
VISPL-TLR-008 Makino VMC or VISPL-TLR-021 ACE MCV-700 Plus

machine_allocation.operation: O5 H7 through holes — WEDM alt

machine_allocation.equipment: Plug gauges, bore gauge, depth micrometer, surface plate, height gauge, CMM if available

drawing_clarifications.topic: Duplicate hole tags A/B and D/E
drawing_clarifications.description: Tags A1-A4 and B1-B4 share identical X/Y coordinates in the hole table. Similarly D1-D4 and E1-E4 share coordinates. These represent compound holes — two diameters at each of four locations, not eight separate holes. Confirm this interpretation with design before issuing the operation sheet.
C45 is capable of being hardened but no hardness or heat-treatment requirement appears on the drawing. Part should be manufactured in normalized condition unless design issues a revised requirement.

No Ra or surface texture symbol on the drawing. ISO 2768-mK general tolerance applies. For a die plate mating face, Ra 1.6 um on ground faces and Ra 3.2 um on milled faces is a reasonable shop standard unless otherwise specified.

drawing_clarifications.topic: Counterbore face — which face receives counterbores
drawing_clarifications.description: Section A-A and Section B-B show the counterbore profiles. Confirm from assembly drawing VI-SR5-25-72-25-R0 which face (top or bottom) receives each counterbore before programming or setting up the machining operations.

All hole coordinates are given to two decimal places. Under the general tolerance table (two-decimal = +- 0.02 mm), each coordinate carries +- 0.02 mm. If a true position geometric tolerance is intended, it should be explicitly called out on the drawing. Confirm with design.

Hole coordinate positions at +- 0.02 mm should ideally be verified on a CMM. If none is available in-house, inspect using calibrated gauge pins and digital height gauge on a granite surface plate. Use CMM at an outside lab for first-off or critical inspection.

critical_precautions: Machine all holes and outside profile from the same coordinate datum — do not re-datum between operations
Grind faces BEFORE machining any counterbore depths — all depths are measured from the finished ground face
Do not finish O5 H7 holes by spot-drilling and drilling alone — ream on CNC
Do not use an ordinary long-lead machine reamer for the O16 H7 blind counterbore
Do not use EDM or WEDM for the blind counterbores
Confirm which face carries the counterbores from Sections A-A and B-B before starting
Confirm the A/B and D/E compound-hole interpretation with design before issuing the operation sheet
Do not use a radial drilling machine for the O5 H7 holes — positional accuracy insufficient
route_summary: Band-saw C45 blank to 100x100x12 mm -> rough face and square on Manford mill -> check flatness -> surface grind to 10.00 +-0.02 mm on Perfect grinder -> finish mill outside to 95.00x95.00 mm -> DRO drill O6.4 through (4 off) and O8.0 through (4 off) on Eifco DRO drilling machine -> produce O10.4 x 6.80 counterbores on Manford mill with piloted counterbore tool -> produce O16 H7 x 8.0 counterbores on Manford mill with boring head (Makino VMC fallback if manual cannot hold tolerance) -> CNC drill and ream O5 H7 through holes (4 off) on Makino VMC -> deburr and edge break -> 100% inspection
